theorems.name: Theorem A (digit-window potentials collapse)
theorems.statement: Let T be a 2-adic table map with a branch (u n + v)/2^e, u = 3 or 5, and an expanding periodic point. No potential V = sum_i f(n_i..n_{i+s-1}) + bounded boundary terms certifies T, for s <= 10 (u=3) and s <= 8 (u=5). Descent forces Phi <= 0 on the x u transducer cycles (pumping); the cycles at odd length k are permuted by x -> u x mod 2^k - 1, so Phi = 0; hence E_f(uh) = E_f(h); exact mod-p rank 2^{s-1} forces f = constant + coboundary, so V = c*len(n) + bounded, which is CM, and Theorem W applies. This covers all 8 cores, K7, 3x+1, 5x+1, and even type-(b) systems.

No type-(c) system was settled. The result is an extension of the wall, which is the second-best outcome the task named.

Theorem W (proved) holds for any residue-class affine map, with or without unit multipliers. It says that a descending potential cannot be coarsely monotone in real size near any expanding periodic point. Its proof is short: integers that shadow the periodic point grow by lambda^k while V has to decrease. For type (c), Corollary W1 makes the failure set dense in an uncountable Cantor set. Corollary W2 then rules out residue x n (+ o(n)), n^gamma e^psi, mantissa factors, digit count, finite sets of counters, and lex/ordinal combinations of these. For unit-multiplier maps, those classes certify exactly the CERT systems.

Theorem A (proved for window width s <= 10 with a x3 branch, s <= 8 with a x5 branch, checked by exact mod-p rank) covers sliding-window digit potentials. The argument combines pumping, the permutation x -> 3x mod 2^k - 1 at odd k, and rigidity, which forces V = c*len(n) + bounded. So these potentials cannot certify any OBST 2-adic system, including all 8 cores, K7, 3x+1, 5x+1 and the type-(b) systems that Theorem H settles. An LP on K7 is infeasible, as the theorem predicts.

For general deterministic automata I only have a reduction to a precise rigidity lemma, which is open. Rewriting encodings of K7 and six cores (YAH style) were built and checked. z3 natural matrix interpretations removed only bookkeeping rules (evidence, not a proof). For mb_s3_27 I found exact homoclinic expanding points that shadow the -5 cycle 10, 20 and 40 times, so Theorem W blocks it too.

prove:schema.summary:
I did not settle any type-(c) system, so the hard success criterion was not met. The result is the second-best outcome the task allowed: the wall is extended. Theorem B1 (cutoff.md) proves that a type-(c) system cannot be reached as a limit of certifiable cut-off systems. If T is of type (c), any table that changes T only near finitely many points is again of type (c), whatever it does on the cut-off region. The thresholds are exact: 3x+1 cut at depth j is certifiable only for j = 2 (type (c) from j = 3, witness cycle -5); K7 is certifiable for j = 2..5 and of type (c) from j = 6 (witness z = -49/17, multiplier 81/64).

The alternative family that does work, window approximants (reset wherever an N-step window expands too much), is certifiable for every unit-multiplier system. For 3x+1 it has an explicit certificate formula uniform in N. It answers the round-3 open question: the distance of 3x+1 to provability, as a fraction of residues, goes to 0, bounded by 2^{0.954N}/2^N. But turning these approximants into a proof requires "every orbit eventually avoids the reset set", and for each N in [4, 26] that statement is equivalent to the Collatz conjecture (W3), so the induction on N is empty. A size-based statement (S_C), that no window longer than C log2 n in the orbit of n expands too much, would imply the conjecture (W4). It is unproved; the numbers fit C near 20.

Part A is fully proved (depth.md). A designed base-2 family (multipliers 3 and 1/2 plus resets, no translation nodes) has an exact formula for the least certificate depth k*. With near-critical loops built from the continued fraction of log2 3, k* grows at least like Q^2 log Q along a subsequence of moduli, and every base-2 multiplier-3 table has k* at most polynomial in Q. The gap between Q^2 log Q and Q^3 is open. New records: k* = 41362 at Q = 256 and 133534 at Q = 512, both with integer witnesses checked by direct iteration; 304506 at Q = 1024 by the formula only. The previous record was 2466. The family is not the S-family, so the round-3 conjecture is proved for this class of tables only.
